common_name: Magnificent Wild Ginger (Chinese Giant Wild Ginger)

planting.note: Set divisions out in spring into rich, consistently moist, well-drained woodland soil in shade, and mulch for winter protection at the colder edge of its range.

directions: This Chinese wild ginger is grown for its large, thick, glossy evergreen leaves, each marked with a bold streak of silver across the leaf surface that makes individual clumps stand out in the woodland garden. In late winter to early spring the plant produces curious black-purple flowers with a wrinkled white throat, held low and often tucked beneath the foliage where collectors part the leaves to view them. Plant in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in light to deep shade, and avoid disturbing the clump once established since it resents root disruption. Give it a sheltered site and winter mulch toward the cooler limits of its hardiness range, where it forms a slowly expanding, long-lived specimen clump.
sources: Hortus Botanicus / botanical garden living collection records
